policy: Permanent minimized regressions of the coordinator-sqlite-merge oracle. A case is never removed or relaxed; a newly found divergence is minimized and appended. Values: a JSON number binds REAL, {"int": "<decimal>"} INTEGER, {"blob": "<base64>"} BLOB, {"real": "-0|Infinity|-Infinity"} the reals JSON cannot spell, a string TEXT, null NULL. Keys 10/30/50/70/90 land in distinct partitions in every layout of two or more; keys below 21 share the first partition in every layout. Column mapping from the design's probe table t(id, amount, dept TEXT): amount -> a (no affinity, as the untyped amount), dept -> x (TEXT, BINARY).

groups.expression-domain-witnesses-trim-cast-ca: external review witnesses W-A, W-B, W-B-join, W-C (design §1.2 and §4.1): projection and predicate, every layout
groups.sqlite-differential-oracle-green: review items 1-9, design N1-N8 and N10-N13, findings confirmed by reading, FROM-less SELECT and -0.0; every layout
groups.sql-render-round-trip-fidelity: catalog DDL round trip (N9 and the type-name mappings); every golden statement also runs through render(parse(Q))
groups.pushdown-soundness-golden-cases: design rev 2 F12: pushdown soundness conditions; every layout
groups.order-dependent-aggregates-exact: design rev 2 F13: scan-order-dependent aggregates compared exactly in canonical layout; every layout
groups.declared-ddl-reference-family: design rev 2 F11: declared DDL the catalog cannot create as declared

cases.statement: SELECT TRIM(MAX(x),'x') AS v FROM t
cases.why: two-argument TRIM ignores its character set in the SELECT combiner (partial-aggregate-combiner.js:439-442)

cases.statement: SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM t HAVING TRIM(MAX(x),'x') = 'abc'
cases.why: the same TRIM in the HAVING evaluator (query-executor-select-aggregation.js:608-609)

cases.statement: SELECT TRIM(MAX(x),'x') AS v FROM t HAVING TRIM(MAX(x),'x') = 'abc'
cases.why: projection and predicate in one statement

cases.statement: SELECT CAST(SUM(a) AS INTEGER) AS v FROM t
cases.why: the design reports the projection alone agrees by value (v=1); the cell's INTEGER class is not carried by the wire

cases.statement: SELECT CAST(SUM(a) AS INTEGER) AS v FROM t HAVING CAST(SUM(a) AS INTEGER) = 1
cases.why: HAVING applies comparison affinity instead of the explicit cast (query-executor-select-aggregation.js:576-582)

cases.source: external review W-B, residual JOIN consumer
cases.statement: SELECT t.id AS c0 FROM t JOIN u ON t.id = u.k AND CAST(t.a + u.v AS INTEGER) = 1 ORDER BY t.id
cases.why: the residual JOIN evaluator applies comparison affinity instead of the cast (residual-predicate-evaluator.js:439-451)

cases.statement: SELECT t.id AS c0 FROM t JOIN u ON t.id = u.k AND CAST(t.a + u.v AS INTEGER) = 1.9 ORDER BY t.id
cases.why: the explicit cast truncates to 1, so = 1.9 holds for no row; a consumer that keeps 1.9 admits both

cases.statement: SELECT t.id FROM t JOIN u ON t.id = u.k WHERE CAST(t.a + u.v AS INTEGER) = 1
cases.why: the same cast as a WHERE conjunct over both tables

cases.statement: SELECT t.id AS c0, CAST(t.a + u.v AS INTEGER) AS c1 FROM t JOIN u ON t.id = u.k ORDER BY t.id
cases.why: the explicit cast in the join's projection

cases.statement: SELECT CASE WHEN '0' THEN SUM(a) ELSE 0 END AS v FROM t
cases.why: JS truthiness Boolean('0') in the SELECT combiner (partial-aggregate-combiner.js:362)

cases.statement: SELECT CASE WHEN '0' THEN SUM(a) ELSE 0 END AS v FROM t HAVING CASE WHEN '0' THEN SUM(a) ELSE 0 END = 0
cases.why: JS truthiness in the HAVING evaluator (query-executor-select-aggregation.js:567)

cases.statement: SELECT id AS c0, x AS c1 FROM t ORDER BY x, id LIMIT 2
cases.why: distributed ORDER BY puts NULL last on ASC (query-executor-select-aggregation.js:251-256)

cases.statement: SELECT id AS c0 FROM t ORDER BY x COLLATE NOCASE, id
cases.why: COLLATE is dropped by the parser and the binary comparator ignores it

cases.statement: SELECT id AS c0 FROM t ORDER BY a, id
cases.why: the comparator does not follow NULL < numeric < TEXT < BLOB

cases.statement: SELECT ROUND(MAX(r), 3) AS v FROM t
cases.why: sqlRound uses toFixed (sql-scalar-functions.js:149): 0.936 instead of 0.937

cases.statement: SELECT MIN(x) AS lo, MAX(x) AS hi FROM t
cases.why: global MIN/MAX combine in UTF-16 code-unit order (partial-aggregate-combiner.js:85-95)

cases.statement: SELECT LENGTH(AVG(i)) AS v FROM t
cases.why: AVG 2.0 renders as '2' once the REAL class is lost: LENGTH 1 instead of 3

cases.statement: SELECT UPPER(MAX(x)) AS v FROM t
cases.why: JS toUpperCase folds non-ASCII; SQLite UPPER without ICU does not

cases.statement: SELECT UPPER(MIN(x)) AS v FROM t
cases.why: JS 'ß'.toUpperCase() is 'SS'

cases.statement: SELECT TRIM(MAX(x)) AS v FROM t
cases.why: JS trim() removes tabs; SQLite TRIM removes spaces only

cases.statement: SELECT ABS(MAX(x)) AS v FROM t
cases.why: ABS('abc') is 0.0 in SQLite

cases.statement: SELECT id AS c0, b AS c1 FROM t ORDER BY id
cases.why: a remote BLOB becomes {type:'Buffer',data} (JSON.stringify without a codec)

cases.statement: SELECT x AS g, SUM(i) AS s FROM t GROUP BY x ORDER BY SUM(i) DESC
cases.why: applyOrderBy keys on clause.expression?.column, so an aggregate term is ignored

cases.statement: SELECT x AS g, COUNT(*) AS c FROM t GROUP BY x ORDER BY MAX(i) DESC
cases.why: the same for MAX

cases.statement: SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(x) AS v FROM t
cases.why: no combine mode, ORIGINAL_RAW_ROWS, then reduceNumericAggregate returns null

cases.statement: SELECT TOTAL(a) AS v FROM t
cases.why: TOTAL is not detected as an aggregate: one row per partition

cases.statement: SELECT typeof(SUM(id)) AS v FROM t
cases.why: an aggregate nested in a non-evaluable function: one row per partition

cases.statement: SELECT id FROM t ORDER BY 1 DESC LIMIT 2
cases.why: positional ORDER BY terms are ignored by the merge

cases.statement: SELECT id FROM t ORDER BY a * 2 DESC LIMIT 2
cases.why: expression ORDER BY terms are ignored by the merge

cases.statement: SELECT id, x FROM t ORDER BY x, id
cases.why: even a single-partition result is re-sorted, NULL last

cases.statement: SELECT name FROM (SELECT x AS name FROM t) ORDER BY name
cases.why: derived table goes to ORIGINAL_RAW_ROWS, then a JS re-sort

cases.statement: SELECT id FROM t WHERE a / 2.0 > 1.2 ORDER BY id
cases.why: decimal literals are rendered as TEXT literals: ((a / '2.0') > '1.2')

cases.statement: SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM t WHERE x = 'a' COLLATE NOCASE
cases.why: the parser drops COLLATE, so partitions compare BINARY

cases.statement: SELECT x AS g, COUNT(*) AS c FROM t GROUP BY x HAVING x LIKE 'a%' ORDER BY x
cases.why: HAVING LIKE is a case-sensitive JS RegExp

cases.statement: SELECT x AS g, COUNT(*) AS c FROM t GROUP BY x HAVING hex(x) = '41' ORDER BY x
cases.why: an unknown HAVING function evaluates to null

cases.statement: SELECT x AS g, COUNT(*) AS c FROM t GROUP BY x HAVING abs(-1) = 1 AND c > 0 ORDER BY c, g
cases.why: HAVING over an output alias is not supported by the split: participant failure

cases.statement: SELECT SUM(DISTINCT a) AS v FROM t
cases.why: front-end refusal of SUM(DISTINCT x): one-sided error

cases.statement: SELECT 1e3 AS v FROM t WHERE id = 10
cases.why: front-end refusal of an exponent literal

cases.statement: SELECT 9007199254740993 AS v FROM t WHERE id = 10
cases.why: an integer literal beyond 2^53

cases.statement: SELECT x'41' AS v FROM t WHERE id = 10
cases.why: front-end refusal of a BLOB literal

cases.statement: SELECT x AS g, COUNT(*) AS c FROM t GROUP BY x
cases.why: [null].join('|') is '', so NULL and '' collide as group keys

cases.statement: SELECT t.id AS c0, u.k AS c1 FROM t JOIN u ON t.x = u.k ORDER BY t.id
cases.why: SQLite applies numeric affinity to the TEXT operand; a JS Map key '1' never equals 1

cases.statement: SELECT id AS c0 FROM t ORDER BY id LIMIT -1
cases.why: buildOverfetchLimit turns a negative LIMIT into LIMIT 0 at the partitions

cases.statement: SELECT id AS c0 FROM t ORDER BY id LIMIT -1 OFFSET 2
cases.why: the same with an OFFSET

cases.statement: SELECT id AS c0 FROM t ORDER BY id LIMIT 3 OFFSET -1
cases.why: SQLite treats a negative OFFSET as 0

cases.source: independent design review 2026-11-17 (regression guard; right today)
cases.statement: SELECT DISTINCT a + 0 AS c0 FROM t ORDER BY a LIMIT 2
cases.why: DISTINCT with LIMIT over one partition holding a=1,1,1,2

cases.statement: SELECT DISTINCT a AS c0 FROM t ORDER BY i LIMIT 3
cases.why: DISTINCT pushed below a per-partition LIMIT

cases.statement: SELECT SUM(r) AS s, TOTAL(r) AS tt, AVG(r) AS av FROM t
cases.why: SQLite's compensated summation gives SUM 1.0, TOTAL 1.0, AVG 0.333...; summing partial sums gives 0.0

cases.statement: SELECT AVG(a) AS v FROM t
cases.why: AVG over [MAX | MAX] is REAL 9.223372036854776e18 in SQLite; a partial SUM overflows

cases.statement: SELECT SUM(a) AS v FROM t
cases.why: SUM over [MIN | MAX, MAX] is INTEGER 9223372036854775806 in SQLite's scan order; the second partition's partial overflows

cases.statement: SELECT SUM(a) AS v FROM t
cases.why: SUM over [MAX | 1, -1] raises integer overflow in SQLite; partial sums MAX and 0 do not

cases.statement: SELECT SUM(a) AS v FROM t
cases.why: SUM over [MAX, 1 | 0.5] is REAL in SQLite; the first partition's partial raises integer overflow

cases.statement: SELECT SUM(a) AS v FROM t
cases.why: SUM over [MAX | MAX] raises integer overflow in SQLite; combining partial sums yields 1.8e19

cases.statement: SELECT MIN(a) AS v FROM t
cases.why: MIN over 1.0 | 1 returns the first minimum in scan order, REAL 1.0; arrival order must not decide

cases.statement: SELECT typeof(MIN(a)) AS v FROM t
cases.why: the storage class of that MIN, visible as text: 'real' in canonical layout

cases.statement: SELECT SUM(i) AS v FROM t WHERE c > '0'
cases.why: canonical layout scans MAX, 1 (overflow); an index scan on c would visit 1, -1, MAX and return MAX

cases.statement: SELECT typeof(MAX(a)) AS v FROM t
cases.why: MAX over 1 | 1.0 keeps the first maximum in canonical layout (integer); an index on a can change it

cases.statement: SELECT Sum( a ) FROM t
cases.why: SQLite names the column "Sum( a )"

cases.statement: SELECT id AS c0 FROM t ORDER BY id LIMIT 5 OFFSET -2
cases.why: a negative OFFSET is zero; an overfetch of LIMIT + OFFSET under-fetches

cases.statement: SELECT id AS c0 FROM t ORDER BY id LIMIT ? OFFSET 2
cases.why: LIMIT ? is a parse error on the candidate (p3)

cases.statement: SELECT id AS c0 FROM t ORDER BY id LIMIT 2 OFFSET ?
cases.why: OFFSET ? is a parse error on the candidate (p3)

cases.statement: SELECT a.id AS c0, b.id AS c1 FROM t a JOIN t b ON a.i = b.i WHERE a.x = 'a' AND b.x = 'b' ORDER BY a.id, b.id
cases.why: one temp table per table reference; each alias keeps its own conjuncts

cases.statement: SELECT rowid AS c0 FROM t ORDER BY rowid
cases.why: rowid aliases are refused in multi-partition plans (design rev 2 §2.2); one partition answers as SQLite

cases.statement: SELECT id AS c0 FROM t WHERE id = '10' COLLATE NOCASE
cases.why: an explicit COLLATE in a key predicate must not change key pruning

cases.statement: SELECT t.id AS c0, u.k AS c1 FROM t JOIN u ON t.x = u.tk COLLATE NOCASE ORDER BY t.id, u.k
cases.why: an explicit non-BINARY COLLATE in ON disables the semi-join key filter

cases.statement: SELECT id FROM t WHERE i > 0 AND x < datetime('now') ORDER BY id LIMIT 2
cases.why: a conjunct kept off the partitions (non-deterministic) must not sit above a pushed partition LIMIT

cases.statement: SELECT z AS g, COUNT(*) AS c FROM t WHERE i > 0 AND x < datetime('now') GROUP BY z ORDER BY z
cases.why: the same conjunct under PARTIAL_AGGREGATE: it must filter before the partition aggregates

cases.statement: SELECT changes() AS c0 FROM t WHERE id = 10
cases.why: connection state on a coordinator read path is refused, never answered from a partition or merge connection

cases.statement: SELECT last_insert_rowid() AS c0 FROM t WHERE id = 10
cases.why: connection state on a coordinator read path is refused

cases.statement: SELECT total_changes() AS c0 FROM t ORDER BY id
cases.why: connection state on a coordinator read path is refused

cases.statement: SELECT id AS c0 FROM t ORDER BY id LIMIT ?
cases.why: LIMIT with a REAL parameter is a datatype mismatch error in SQLite

cases.statement: SELECT id AS c0 FROM t ORDER BY id LIMIT ?
cases.why: LIMIT with TEXT '2' is LIMIT 2 in SQLite

cases.statement: SELECT 1 AS c0 LIMIT 0
cases.why: a FROM-less SELECT drops its LIMIT

cases.statement: SELECT 2 AS c0 ORDER BY 1 LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1
cases.why: a FROM-less SELECT drops its ORDER BY, LIMIT and OFFSET

cases.statement: SELECT r AS c0, a AS c1 FROM t ORDER BY id
cases.why: -0.0 survives in an untyped column but not in a REAL one; a frame turns -0 into 0

cases.statement: SELECT MIN(a) AS v, typeof(MIN(a)) AS t FROM t
cases.why: a projection of an aggregate next to a function of an aggregate drops a result column

cases.statement: SELECT id AS c0 FROM t WHERE x LIKE 'a!%%' ESCAPE '!' ORDER BY id
cases.why: the renderer drops ESCAPE, so the partitions match 'a!%%' literally

cases.ddl: CREATE TABLE g9 (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT COLLATE NOCASE, tail TEXT COLLATE RTRIM)
cases.why: formatDerivedColumn stores no collation and the partition DDL renderer emits none

cases.ddl: CREATE TABLE gw (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, nu NUMERIC, de DECIMAL(10,2), d DATE, dt DATETIME, ts TIMESTAMP, bo BOOLEAN, fl FLOAT, vc VARCHAR(10), bi BIGINT)
cases.why: normalizeDataType maps NUMERIC/DECIMAL to REAL, DATE/DATETIME/TIMESTAMP to TEXT, BOOLEAN to INTEGER

cases.ddl: CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, i INTEGER, r REAL, n NUMERIC, x TEXT, c TEXT COLLATE NOCASE, z TEXT COLLATE RTRIM, b BLOB, a)
cases.why: a column without a type is refused by the front end, and NUMERIC and both COLLATE clauses are lost

cases.ddl: CREATE TABLE u (k INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tk TEXT COLLATE NOCASE, v)
cases.why: a column without a type is refused by the front end, and the COLLATE clause is lost

cases.ddl: CREATE TABLE gu (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, un, label TEXT)
cases.why: a bare untyped column is SQLite DDL; the front end refuses it with an untyped error

cases.ddl: CREATE TABLE gb (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, ub UNSIGNED BIG INT, vc VARCHAR(20))
cases.why: UNSIGNED BIG INT is SQLite DDL (INTEGER affinity); the front end refuses it with an untyped error

cases.ddl: CREATE TABLE w (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, nu NUMERIC, de DECIMAL(10,2), bo BOOLEAN, d DATE, ts TIMESTAMP, vc VARCHAR(20))
cases.why: the F11 family's table: the catalog must create each declared type name with SQLite's affinity for it
